cards.text: Ezekiel, a prophet living in exile with his people, tells what happened next. In the twenty-fifth year of their exile, fourteen years after Jerusalem was struck down, the hand of the LORD is upon him. On that very day, He takes Ezekiel somewhere.

cards.question: In visions of God, where does the LORD take the exiled Ezekiel?

cards.text: He sets Ezekiel on a very high mountain, and on its southern slope is a structure that looks like a city. Me, I have to hop, base and all, just to see over a mixing bowl.
So He takes Ezekiel there, and standing in the gateway is a man whose appearance is like bronze. One look and you know this is NOT your regular tour guide.

cards.question: The bronze-looking man in the gateway is holding something in his hand. What is it?

answers.text: A linen cord and a measuring rod
A scroll and a writing reed
A trumpet and a burning lamp

cards.text: Then the man calls him “Son of man” and tells him, “look with your eyes, hear with your ears…” I half-listened to an oven timer once, friend, and I'm STILL scraping that batch off the pan.

cards.question: The man tells Ezekiel to look, listen and pay close attention. Why does the man say Ezekiel has been brought here?

answers.text: To see everything the man will show him
To build a new city on the mountain
To guard the gateway with the man

cards.question: The man tells Ezekiel to keep everything he sees to himself.

cards.text: So Ezekiel starts looking. The first thing he sees is a wall running all the way around the temple area.

cards.question: The man measures the wall around the temple area.

cards.text: The man's measuring rod is six long cubits, and the wall comes out one rod thick and one rod high. This man measures EVERYTHING, and my measuring is a scoop, a squint and a prayer.

Then he climbs the steps of the gate facing east and measures it piece by piece: its threshold, its gate chambers, three on each side, its portico and its gateposts. It has windows all around the inside, and its side pillars are decorated with palm trees.

cards.question: When the man finishes measuring the east gate, what does he do with Ezekiel next?

answers.text: Brings him into the outer court
Sends him back down the mountain
Leaves him waiting at the east gate

cards.text: The outer court has a pavement all around it, with thirty chambers facing the pavement. The man measures the gates facing north and south too, and each one matches the east gate, with seven steps leading up to it.

Next he brings Ezekiel into the inner court through the south gate and measures the inner gates on the south, east and north, each with eight steps. Every gate comes out fifty cubits long and twenty-five wide, all SIX of them, and I can't get two cookies to match.

In each of the inner gateways, by the portico, there's a chamber with a doorway, and it's there for a job with the offerings. That room's got one job, which is more than I could say for my old junk drawer.

cards.question: In the chamber by each inner gateway's portico, the ___ offering was to be washed.
Inside the portico of the gateway are two tables on each side. What were those tables for?

cards.text: Count them up: four tables inside the gateway and four outside by the north gate, eight in all. There are also four tables of dressed stone holding the tools for the sacrifices, and double-pronged hooks fastened all around the inside of the room.
In the inner court there are two chambers: one beside the north gate facing south, and one beside the south gate facing north.

cards.question: The man says the two chambers in the inner court are for priests. What do the priests in the south-facing chamber keep charge of?
The man says the north-facing chamber is for the priests who keep charge of the altar.
The man says the priests who keep charge of the altar are the sons of Zadok. What does he say sets them apart from the other Levites?

answers.text: Only they may approach the LORD to minister
Only they may live inside the holy city
Only they may stand guard at the outer gates

cards.text: Next the man measures the inner court: square, a hundred cubits long and a hundred wide, with the altar in front of the temple. My cookies are supposed to be ROUND, friend, and some days they can't even pull THAT off.

Then the man brings Ezekiel to the portico of the temple itself, with ten steps leading up to it and columns by the side pillars, one on each side. That's where we'll leave Ezekiel for now, friend, because this tour is just getting started.
